$comment: Hand-edited (docs/SCHEMA.md), except geometry, geometry_confidence, geometry_method and georeference, which `make past` rebuilds from trace.json. Work in progress: the Phase 2a pilot.

properties.name: Oakland Mole
properties.geometry_method: Traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (5 hand-read points). The centre of the mole's bundle of tracks, from the ferry slips to the shore at Seventh Street. The 1915 San Francisco sheet, corrected (sf1915-bay), puts the terminal within about 20 m of the 1949 sheet's.

properties.name: Alameda Mole
properties.geometry_method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (8 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (8 hand-read points); the sheet corrected by a shift on 3 control points (Yerba Buena Island on the 1949 Oakland West sheet; +74 m E, +213 m N, RMS 44.8 m). The railroad on the south jetty of the estuary's Deep Water Channel, from the ferry terminal to the junction at Alameda's west shore. Filled over by 1949, so traced from 1915.

properties.name: Oakland Mole to Sixteenth Street Station
properties.geometry_method: Joined to sp-oakland-mole at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (4 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points). The Southern Pacific main line from the mole through the West Oakland yard to Sixteenth Street Station, as the 1949 sheet draws it; the yard's many tracks make the line's exact track uncertain.

sources.note: Before 1939 the Berkeley lines ran from Oakland Pier over the elevated tracks at Sixteenth Street station.

properties.notes: The Southern Pacific's main line, shared with its steam trains; its own dates aren't recorded here.

properties.name: Sixteenth Street Station to 34th Street
properties.geometry_method: Joined to sp-mole-16th-st at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (4 hand-read points). Northeast from Sixteenth Street Station, then north at Wood Street to 34th Street.

sources.note: From 1939, Berkeley trains from the bridge joined the old Berkeley main line at 32nd Street.

properties.name: Wood Street, 34th Street to Ninth Street junction
properties.geometry_method: Joined to sp-16th-st-34th-st at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (7 hand-read points). North along the tracks by Wood Street from 34th Street, curving northeast to the junction at Stanford Avenue and Hollis Street (Ninth Street junction), where the 1949 sheet shows the track splitting north (Ninth Street line) and northeast (Stanford Avenue).

sources.note: "Between the wye and Ninth Street junction operations are over private right of way."
"relocation of existing railway tracks in Wood Street, north of 34th Street"

properties.name: Stanford Avenue
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Stanford Avenue centerline from Hollis Street to Adeline Street (1781 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). The private right of way ran beside the avenue (on its south side, as the 1949 sheet draws it); drawn on the avenue's centerline.

sources.note: From Ninth Street junction "principally over open track in private right of way along Stanford Avenue and Adeline Street, through a portion of Emeryville and North Oakland to Berkeley".

properties.name: Adeline Street
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Adeline Street centerline from Stanford Avenue to Shattuck Avenue (1460 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). Private right of way along Adeline Street; drawn on the street's centerline.

sources.note: "over private right of way along Adeline Street to Shattuck Avenue"

properties.name: Shattuck Avenue, Adeline Street to Bancroft Way
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Shattuck Avenue centerline from Adeline Street to Bancroft Way (875 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). Paved-in right of way in Shattuck Avenue.

sources.note: "along Shattuck Avenue in paved-in right of way to Bancroft Avenue"

properties.name: Shattuck Avenue, Bancroft Way to Vine Street
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Shattuck Avenue centerline from Bancroft Way to Vine Street (1416 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915). In the paved street.

sources.note: "in paved street along Shattuck Avenue to a point between Vine and Rose Street"

properties.name: Shattuck Avenue to Sutter Street
properties.geometry_method: Joined to sp-shattuck-ave-north at its end; then along today's Henry Street centerline from Shattuck Avenue to Sutter Street (342 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Richmond 1:24,000 (1949). The sources call this "connecting private right of way" without placing it; drawn along Henry Street, which the 1941 substitute bus used, as a stand-in, and dashed.

sources.note: "thence over private right of way and paved street to a terminus at Thousand Oaks Station at Colusa Street and Solano Avenue"
Key System's F line was let run "north along Shattuck Avenue and Sutter Street, together with connecting private right of way, over tracks formerly used by Interurban Electric Railway Company".

properties.name: Sutter Street to Northbrae Station
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Sutter Street centerline from Henry Street to Hopkins Street (361 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Richmond 1:24,000 (1949). In Sutter Street.

sources.note: "Northbrae station, located at the intersection of Sutter and Hopkins Streets"

properties.name: Northbrae Station through the Northbrae Tunnel to The Alameda
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Sutter Street centerline from Hopkins Street to Solano Avenue (71 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); then along today's Solano Avenue centerline from Sutter Street to The Alameda (552 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Richmond 1:24,000 (1949). Private right of way from Northbrae Station through the Northbrae Tunnel, which carries Solano Avenue today, to The Alameda.

sources.note: "a tunnel 465 ft. long in North Berkeley, where the line passes under a point from which several streets radiate"
"Beyond Northbrae the rail line followed unpaved private right of way through the tunnel to The Alameda, a distance of less than one-half mile."

properties.notes: The 465-ft tunnel under The Circle is part of this segment; drawn as surface for now.

properties.name: Solano Avenue, The Alameda to Thousand Oaks Station
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Solano Avenue centerline from The Alameda to Colusa Avenue (218 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Richmond 1:24,000 (1949). In Solano Avenue.

sources.note: "thence over private right of way and paved street to a terminus at Thousand Oaks Station at Colusa Street and Solano Avenue"

properties.name: Ninth Street junction to Heinz Avenue, Emeryville
properties.geometry_method: Joined to sp-wood-st at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (8 hand-read points). North from Ninth Street junction through Emeryville to Heinz Avenue, read by hand where the 1949 sheet draws the track among others.

sources.note: "from Thousand Oaks station along Solano Avenue across San Pablo Avenue, thence south over private right of way to Harrison Street, thence in paved street along Ninth Street through West Berkeley to Heinz Avenue, thence generally over private right of way through Emeryville to the … Bay Bridge"

properties.name: Ninth Street, Heinz Avenue to Harrison Street
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Ninth Street centerline from Heinz Avenue to Harrison Street (3198 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Richmond 1:24,000 (1949). In Ninth Street.

sources.note: "from Thousand Oaks station along Solano Avenue across San Pablo Avenue, thence south over private right of way to Harrison Street, thence in paved street along Ninth Street through West Berkeley to Heinz Avenue, thence generally over private right of way through Emeryville to the … Bay Bridge"

properties.name: Solano Avenue, Thousand Oaks Station to San Pablo Avenue
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Solano Avenue centerline from Colusa Avenue to San Pablo Avenue (1710 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Richmond 1:24,000 (1949). In Solano Avenue, across San Pablo Avenue.

sources.note: "from Thousand Oaks station along Solano Avenue across San Pablo Avenue, thence south over private right of way to Harrison Street, thence in paved street along Ninth Street through West Berkeley to Heinz Avenue, thence generally over private right of way through Emeryville to the … Bay Bridge"

properties.name: Albany, Solano Avenue to Harrison Street
properties.geometry_method: Joined to sp-ninth-st at its end; then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (8 hand-read points); then joined to sp-solano-ave-west at its end; the sheet corrected by a shift on 3 control points (Yerba Buena Island on the 1949 Oakland West sheet; +74 m E, +213 m N, RMS 44.8 m). The 1915 sheet draws a railroad here, west of San Pablo Avenue, but places it only roughly; its north end stops short of Solano Avenue on the sheet, and the last stretch to Solano Avenue is joined straight.

sources.note: "from Thousand Oaks station along Solano Avenue across San Pablo Avenue, thence south over private right of way to Harrison Street, thence in paved street along Ninth Street through West Berkeley to Heinz Avenue, thence generally over private right of way through Emeryville to the … Bay Bridge"
